name: pihole-v6-unbound
description: This Docker deployment runs both Pi-Hole version 6 and Unbound in a single container. The base image for the container is the official Pi-Hole docker container, with an extra build step added to install the Unbound resolver directly into to the container based on instructions provided directly by the Pi-Hole team.

paths.name: /etc/pihole
paths.description: Pi-hole v6 moves all configuration into this folder.

paths.name: /etc/dnsmasq.d
paths.description: This path is no longer necessary. Pi-hole V6 moves all config to the /etc/pihole/pihole.toml file.

ports.name: Port 53 TCP
ports.description: Port 53 TCP/UDP used for DNS traffic

ports.name: Port 53 UDP
ports.description: Port 53 TCP/UDP used for DNS traffic

ports.name: Unbound Port
ports.description: Used internally by PiHole to route DNS requests to unbound.

ports.name: DHCP Server Port
ports.description: Set to 67 if using Pi-hole as your DHCP server

ports.name: NTP Server Port(Time)
ports.description: Set to 123 if you are using Pi-hole as your NTP server and add--cap-add=SYS_TIME to Extra Parameters

variables.name: Web Password
variables.description: Not setting this will result in a random password being generated.

variables.name: PiHole DNS servers
variables.description: Set the DNS server(s) that Pi-hole uses seperated by semi-colons. Since we are using unbound, should be set to 127.0.0.1#5335

variables.name: DNSSEC
variables.description: Set to true to enable DNSSEC. Will add to logs.

variables.name: Enable /dnsmasq.d
variables.description: Load custom user configuration files from /etc/dnsmasq.d/

variables.name: DNSMASQ Config Lines
variables.description: Use this to add dnsmasq config lines without adding .conf files. Lines should be seperated with a semi-colon.

variables.name: Rev Server
variables.description: Used to forward DNS requests to local records(router) for resolution. Use the following format: true,192.168.0.0/24,192.168.0.1#53,lan
